hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence and big accuracy drops (runs 12, 13, 14, 19).
At very small learning rates, 243 epochs of Adam undertrain, so a larger rate helps (runs 1, 2, 10).
Deeper networks are less stable at high learning rates (run 48).
Removing a layer stabilizes training when the learning rate is high (runs 53, 59, 60).
Narrower networks tolerate large learning rates better (runs 79, 80, 73).
Strong L2 regularization underfits, so relaxing it helps (run 91).
Further strengthening an already heavy penalty worsens underfitting (runs 85, 86).
Wide networks diverge more readily with larger learning rates (runs 19, 7).
Three-layer networks are the most sensitive to learning rate increases (runs 12, 6, 15).
Wider layers amplify the instability at high learning rates (run 68).
